# gh-337/13 — Generated files regenerate instead of resolving

### Goal

A base update whose conflicts are all generated files is finished by norn with no agent: it takes the base side, runs the mapped commands and commits the merge with `Norn-Regenerated`. A branch holding only its spec folder takes the base side with no agent and no config (#126). On the light path a regenerated merge counts as clean.

`bun run test` and `bun run typecheck`: green (test#1 on this head).

### Easy to miss

- `abortMerge` is `reset --hard HEAD` + `clean -fd`, not `merge --abort`: `merge --abort` refuses once a command has rewritten a staged path. This is safe only because `update` refuses a dirty worktree before it merges.
- Every update now merges with `keepConflicts` and aborts through `abortMerge`, so the git argv of a plain conflict changed. `test/e2e/transcripts/base-sync.txt` was rewritten with `NORN_TRANSCRIPT_UPDATE=1` as the intended change. The rewrite also picked up `rev-parse refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}` lines that earlier slices' observe changes had left unpinned.
- Spec-folder-only means every non-merge commit on the first-parent line since the base touches only the spec folder, and every merge is a norn base update (`Norn-Tick` trailer and an `Update <story> from` subject). A merge of the remote branch could carry a person's work, so it disqualifies the branch. Any conflict inside the spec folder goes to resolve.
- The light path's clean check needs the trailer and every remerge-diff path matched by the current mapping. Without a mapping, nothing counts as regenerated.

### Not proven yet

- AC8 is for the agent verifier to read. No test runs `bun run schema:emit` as a regenerate command in a fresh worktree. A worktree without `node_modules` would make the command fail, and the update then goes to resolve with the output: safe, but no faster.

### Notes

- The glob matcher lives in core (`packages/core/src/regenerate.ts`, `Bun.Glob`), so act and the light path read the same mapping. Core already uses `Bun.CryptoHasher`, and the purity lint allows it.
- The classify receipt's `base` gained `regenerated` (paths taken from the base, also on a spec-folder-only merge) and `regenerate.output` (on a conflict). The receipt detail names which of the two happened.
- A config error for a missing required field now names the field (`` `regenerate.0.run` is required ``) instead of the list.
- Friction: none.
- Review #1 (approve) left one minor note for the person: `docs/reference.md` is only partly generated (`docs:emit` rewrites its generated block), so taking the base side of it on a conflict in its hand-written part drops the story's prose there, and the light path then counts that merge `clean`. The mapping is what user story 68 asks; narrowing it is the person's call.
